correctness.rationale: For every integer d>=2, iteration gives G_d(c)=h_d(c^(d-1)) with h_d(t)=t(t+1)^d+1. The derivative factorization h_d'(t)=(t+1)^(d-1)((d+1)t+1) yields Res(h_d,h_d')=(d+1)^(d+1)-d^d. The composition resultant for h_d(c^(d-1)) gives the exact power (d-1)^(d^2-1), the factor R_d^(d-1), and sign (-1)^(d+1). The valuation formula follows by taking p-adic valuations. A standalone standard-library script verifies exact Sylvester determinants for d=2,...,7; these finite checks are supplementary, not the proof.

originality.rationale: The retained claim is the explicit closed polynomial-discriminant formula for the exact-period-three critical-orbit polynomial and its exact prime-valuation consequence. Hutz–Towsley define the same polynomial, study its discriminant as a transversality invariant, and give examples for d=5 and d=7, but their inspected full text does not state the general formula. Buff treats the equivalent transformed polynomial and its irreducibility; Goksel treats related irreducibility and arithmetic questions. No directly covering formula was found in bounded literature and claim-index searches. The result is a short specialization of classical resultant identities, so priority against unindexed or unpublished derivations is not absolute.
residual_risks: The formula is a short application of classical resultant identities to a known polynomial, so an unindexed prior derivation or an obvious corollary in another source may exist.
The bounded searches and inspected literature do not prove absolute novelty or uniqueness.
The claim concerns the polynomial discriminant only; it does not identify number-field discriminants when the polynomial is reducible.

value.rationale: The discriminant is the natural arithmetic invariant controlling repeated roots after reduction modulo primes, and Hutz–Towsley use it to detect finite-characteristic transversality failure. The formula gives exact prime support and exact valuations for the entire period-three family in every degree, generalizing the paper's isolated d=5 and d=7 factorizations. This is useful for studying ramification and reduction of critical-orbit parameter polynomials; the value is the closed all-degree invariant, not novelty of the resultant method.
